47:## A/harness/ (written by the harness agent or copied from a previous run)
48:- Optional `args.harness_from` is a non-empty directory path to a previous run's `A/harness/`, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory. After a successful fresh box probe, the pipeline copies the exact bytes of `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` into the current `A/harness/` and skips the initial harness agent call. If present, `run_evaluation.sh` is copied too. Missing or unreadable required scripts, or an invalid argument, fail reproduce with `error_class: parse`; there is no fallback harness generation. Without this argument, harness generation is unchanged.
49-- Reuse writes script-owned `C/harness_source.json` as `{source, files}`. `source` is the absolute source harness directory; `files` maps each copied filename to `{sha256, modified}`. `sha256` is the lowercase 64-digit SHA-256 of the exact original copied bytes and remains unchanged after repair. `modified` starts false and becomes true after an accepted repair of that script, before its upload/rerun, even if that rerun fails. Reuse permits the same bounded setup and anchor repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors) as generated harnesses; every repair receives the fresh probe. Reuse adds no stage facts and does not reuse probe results, measurements, or stock verification.
50-- `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh`, `run_command.sh` are bash scripts. The pipeline invokes them as `bash harness/<name>` from one fresh `/tmp/m5-<uuid>` directory on the already-running operator-managed box. They share that directory across reproduce and profile. No dev lifecycle commands are issued. `BOX` and `FETCH` are inherited unchanged by `boxrun.sh`, including injected executables.
51-- Harness uploads (the initial upload of every harness script, and the re-upload of rewritten scripts after each accepted repair) use the implement upload encoding, so no process argument or remote command line grows with script size. For each script, the upload truncates `harness/<name>` (`: > harness/<name>`) and then appends its base64 in independently decodable chunks of at most 24,576 characters (`printf %s <chunk> | base64 -d >> harness/<name>`); an empty script is created empty. These lines are batched in order into boxrun commands below 32,768 characters. Every batch begins with `set -e` and `mkdir -p harness out`, runs as operation `upload` under the setup budget, and has its own receipt. A batch that fails (nonzero exit, failed fetch, missing receipt, or a timeout after its identical retry) ends the upload: later batches are not sent and the harness script does not run, and the step fails as a failed upload does today (`infra`, or `timeout` on a timeout). After all batches succeed, the uploaded files are byte-identical to the local harness files. A harness small enough for one batch uploads in exactly one `upload` command, as before. Run evidence (blind-01 run5, 2026-10-31): the single upload command exceeded the operating system's 131,072-byte limit on one argument, spawning boxrun failed with E2BIG before any receipt was written, and reproduce stopped with `infra` before setup ran.
52-- `setup.sh` installs/builds the exact published baseline in the stock image; sudo is allowed only for apt. Published source/configuration stays under `baseline-published/`; inputs stay under `data/`. Setup builds and checks only the baseline; the fixed pipeline profiler owns profiling tools and installation. Setup must tolerate one retry in the same directory. Tuning is deferred.
53-- `run_anchors.sh` runs the published protocol at the intake's representative scale and writes `out/anchors_measured.json` as an object mapping each intake item ID (anchors and references) to a finite measured number; with an empty anchors.json it still runs the published command and writes `{}`. Missing or non-numeric measurements fail the corresponding anchor; booleans and nonfinite values count as non-numeric. Additional measurements are ignored for scoring.
54-- `run_command.sh` contains only the exact measured baseline command and complete environment at the representative scale, including working directory, arguments, CUDA visibility and GPU count. It runs the published binary, saves its output for anchor parsing, and propagates its exit status. `run_anchors.sh` invokes `bash harness/run_command.sh` from the shared working directory without overriding its environment or duplicating the command. Profiling invokes that same file from that same directory. No agent writes profiling scripts or profile outputs.

Setup permits up to four repairs (`harness-repair`) and anchors up to two (`anchors-repair`) after a nonzero exit, with the same role/model. Each repair receives the failure class and at most the last 200 log lines of the latest failed attempt, and its prompt states its attempt number and the step's limit (`repair attempt <n> of <limit>`). Each later repair runs only after the previous repaired script ran and failed again (nonzero exit or output-gate error); a declined (null) repair, an infrastructure or fetch failure, or a failed upload ends the step. Owner direction 2026-10-30: finish experiments rather than stop them on a fixable failure; a blind run spent its one setup repair on a build-dependency failure, the repair worked, and setup then failed on a different import error that a single repair could not reach. U46 run evidence (blind-01 run7, 2026-10-31): setup spent both of its two repairs on successive script errors; each repair's log tail held its error, each repair targeted it and none regressed, a static check before upload would have caught none, and setup reruns reuse the materials already fetched and verified, so an attempt after a repair costs tens of seconds; an authorized reader judged more repairs of the same kind the smallest sufficient fix. Anchors keep two repairs until a run shows otherwise. The setup repair may rewrite only `setup.sh`. The anchors step executes `run_anchors.sh` and the `run_command.sh` it invokes, so the anchors repair may rewrite either or both and nothing else; a rewritten `run_command.sh` still obeys every `run_command.sh` rule above, and the anchors repair prompt states this. After each repair every rewritten script is recopied, then the step reruns once, with its budget resolved at the rerun's start (U47). Under reuse, an accepted anchors repair marks `modified` true for each of the two scripts whose bytes it changed. Infrastructure/fetch failures do not trigger repairs. Timeouts use the same repairs (the step's own limit), never an extra one. Repair prompts include budget seconds, measured wall seconds and max(0, wall_s-budget_s) overrun seconds. Profiling has no agent repair or execution retry; output/gate failures stop downstream work.

61-## A/results/reproduce/ and deterministic anchor scoring
62-- Every reproduce box command fetches remote `out/` into `A/results/reproduce/out/`, and its `<receipt-id>.log` into `A/results/reproduce/`. Logs remain in the agent view. The local fetched `out/` is cleared before each command to prevent stale measurements. The final copy contains the anchor run's outputs. When reproduce passes, the pipeline freezes those outputs on the box: through boxrun, as operation `reproduce-freeze` under the `setup` budget, it runs `test ! -e reproduce-out` and then `cp -a out reproduce-out` in the shared run directory. Like every reproduce command, its fetch replaces `A/results/reproduce/out/`, so that local copy and remote `reproduce-out/` hold the same outputs: the baseline outputs the seal and the test author read. Later stages never write to `reproduce-out/`; remote `out/` after reproduce also collects profiler and probe outputs and further runs of the baseline command, which are not baseline outputs. A failed `reproduce-freeze` (nonzero exit, failed fetch, or timeout) fails reproduce with `error_class: infra`, or `timeout` on a timeout, without repair.
63-- `python3 m5/score_anchors.py <anchors.json> <measured.json> <out.json>` writes an atomic JSON object with exact keys `anchors`, `anchors_passed`, `anchors_total`, `all_passed`, `references_total`.
64-  - `anchors` preserves intake order and contains `{id, kind, published_value, measured_value, tolerance, passed}` for every item, with `kind` `"anchor"` or `"reference"`. Items with `uncertainty` keep it unchanged in their row. Reference rows have `passed: null` and `difference` (measured minus published, or null when unmeasured); an unmeasured reference row has `reason` `missing` or `non_numeric` and is never a failure. `tolerance` preserves its input form; `passed` is boolean. Missing or non-numeric measurements are represented by `measured_value: null`. Failed rows additionally contain `reason`: `unknown_comparison`, `missing`, `non_numeric`, `out_of_tolerance` (for `"=="`), or `threshold_not_met` (for inequalities). Unknown comparisons take precedence over measurement failures; missing measurements take precedence over non-numeric measurements. Passing rows have no `reason` field.
65-  - `anchors_passed` and `anchors_total` count anchors only and `references_total` counts references; all are nonnegative integers. `all_passed` is true exactly when every anchor passed, including when there are none. An empty array is valid. Duplicate IDs, invalid published values, invalid tolerances or uncertainties, and nonfinite calculated equality differences/tolerances are parse errors. Unknown comparisons and missing/non-numeric measurements are anchor failures rather than parse errors.
66-  - Exit 0 means every anchor passed; exit 4 means at least one anchor failed; exit 1 means invalid/missing input or an output write failure. Invalid input does not produce a new score file. Diagnostics contain no input content.
67-- The pipeline writes the score to `A/results/reproduce/anchors_scored.json`.
68-- Reproduce facts are `{anchors_passed, anchors_total, stock_verified, tuned_control_valid}` plus common `tokens_known` and `gpu_busy_known`. Counts remain null until scoring succeeds; `stock_verified` is true only after setup exits 0; `tuned_control_valid` remains null. The gate passes only when stock is verified and every anchor passes (true with no anchors). `run_valid` is true/false when anchor scoring passes/fails with at least one anchor, and null when there are no anchors.

70-## A/results/profile/ and A/profile-packet.json
71-- Profile fetches remote `out/` to `A/results/profile/out/`; logs are `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. Its inputs are therefore under `A/results/profile/out/profile/`. Remote `out/profile/` is cleared before profiling to prevent stale evidence from passing.
72-- The pipeline uploads trusted `m5/profile_nsys.sh`, `m5/profile_summarise.py` and the collected probe into remote `profiler/`. Through boxrun, it invokes `bash profiler/profile_nsys.sh harness/run_command.sh out/profile <budget_s>`. The profiler reuses `nsys` from PATH or NVIDIA installation paths. Otherwise it tries `nsight-systems-cli` with apt using only source files listed by the probe, without enabling commented repositories or adding sources. If unavailable, it downloads the official Ubuntu 22.04 amd64 CLI package `NsightSystems-linux-cli-public-2025.3.1.90-3582212.deb` from `https://developer.download.nvidia.com/devtools/repos/ubuntu2204/amd64/` into a temporary directory outside `out/` that is removed after installation (the package never reaches `out/` or fetched results), verifies the SHA-256 pinned in the script, installs with `sudo -n dpkg -i` and runs `sudo -n apt-get -f install -y` for dependencies using the image's existing sources without adding repositories. This fixed profiler installation is an exception to the setup-script installation restrictions above. The profiler prepends the discovered Nsight binary directory to PATH. Missing tools, installation failures and collection/export failures emit `M5_PROFILER_INFRA`, write `out/profile/infra.json`, and exit 2; the pipeline classifies these as `infra` without agent calls.
73-- Collection uses `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none` around the shared command without modifying its environment. An inner launcher measures only that command with a monotonic clock; installation, profiler finalization and CSV export are excluded. The command's output is preserved in `baseline.log` as well as its own saved logs. Export uses `nsys stats --report cuda_gpu_kern_sum,cuda_gpu_mem_time_sum,cuda_api_sum --format csv`. Raw report, CSV files, tool version, export log, `raw_wall_s.json` and `gpu_util_raw.jsonl` remain in `out/profile/`.
74-- `python3 m5/profile_summarise.py <out_dir>` deterministically writes the three existing profile files. CSV total time/duration units ns, us/µs, ms and s are converted to seconds. Known Nsight skips for absent kernel/memory/API activity count as zero; missing or malformed reports fail parsing. A report is a known skip when its CSV file carries Nsight's `SKIPPED` line and no header row, or when its CSV file is absent, empty or whitespace-only and `stats.log` in the same directory states that the report does not contain its own activity: `does not contain CUDA kernel data` for `stats_cuda_gpu_kern_sum.csv`, `does not contain GPU memory data` for `stats_cuda_gpu_mem_time_sum.csv`, and `does not contain CUDA trace data` for `stats_cuda_api_sum.csv` (U48). These are Nsight's own wordings; the earlier phrases `CUDA memory data` and `CUDA API data` never occur in Nsight output and no longer count as statements. Nsight Systems 2025 writes an empty file for a skipped report where earlier versions wrote none. An absent, empty or whitespace-only file without that statement for its own activity, and any other missing or malformed report, still fails parsing. Run evidence (blind-01 run9, 2026-11-01): the baseline ran to completion under the profiler with no CUDA activity and no capture problem; Nsight 2025 logged the three skips and wrote three empty summary files, and the summariser failed on a missing CSV header, so profile stopped with `parse` instead of reaching its numeric gate. Replay of the merged U48 summariser on run9's saved files (2026-11-01) still failed: Nsight states the memory and API skips as `GPU memory data` and `CUDA trace data`; with those wordings the summariser exits 0 and the gate reports `numeric` (other host time within 2% of total wall). Five rows are emitted: `kernels` (compute), `memcpy H2D` (transfer), `memcpy D2H` (transfer), `CUDA API host time` (other), and `other host time` (other). GPU seconds retain the raw kernel/transfer sums; host GPU seconds are null. Aggregate CSV reports do not identify critical-path intervals: if the four reported sums exceed measured wall, their wall allocations are scaled proportionally to fit. Other host time is the nonnegative wall remainder. These allocations are an aggregate approximation, not measured exclusive phase durations. No stage timestamps are invented; aggregate rows omit `start_s`, so stage utilisation remains null. No bound uses stage utilisation; same-GPU headroom comes from the concurrency probe.
75-- `stages.json` is an array of `{stage, wall_s, gpu_s}`, optionally including `kind`: `compute`, `transfer`, or `other`, and `start_s`: finite nonnegative elapsed seconds sharing the telemetry clock. Fixed profiler supplies `kind`; legacy rows without it remain accepted. `stage` is a non-empty string; `wall_s` is finite nonnegative seconds; `gpu_s` is finite nonnegative seconds or null and must be present. Fixed profiler wall allocations sum to measured wall without exceeding it; overlapping aggregate durations use the approximation above. Extra input fields are not copied to the packet. Empty arrays parse but fail the numeric gate.
76-- `total_wall_s.json` is an object with finite positive numeric `total_wall_s` in seconds. The sum of stage wall times must also be finite.
77-- `gpu_util.json` is an array of `{t, util}` samples collected with `nvidia-smi` during the measured run. `t` is finite nonnegative elapsed seconds; `util` is a finite GPU utilisation percentage in [0,100]. The fixed sampler records the mean across GPUs returned by nvidia-smi, then the summarizer retains only samples during the shared command and rebases monotonic timestamps to its start. A sample with zero utilisation is valid. Empty arrays parse but fail the numeric gate; missing files or malformed samples fail parsing.
78-- The deterministic pipeline writes `A/profile-packet.json` with exact keys:
79-  - `stages`: the validated timing rows, preserving optional `kind`, each augmented with `wall_fraction = min(1, wall_s / total_wall_s)`, `start_s`, and `mean_gpu_util` (fraction in [0,1], or null). When supplied, `start_s` must be measured on the telemetry clock. Legacy rows without `start_s` record null start and utilisation; stage order does not establish a measured telemetry window. Stage endpoints must remain finite. Stage utilisation is the arithmetic mean of telemetry percentages divided by 100 in `[start_s, start_s + wall_s)`; no samples means null. Never substitute GPU busy seconds for utilisation;
80-  - `total_wall_s`: the measured total;
81-  - `timed_fraction = min(1, sum(stage.wall_s) / total_wall_s)`;
82-  - `gpu_telemetry`: true only when the validated `gpu_util.json` array is non-empty; stage `gpu_s` values do not establish telemetry.
83-  - `gpu_count`: `C/box.json.gpu_count` when nonnegative integer, otherwise count parsed from allocation `type` (`gpu_<N>x_...`), otherwise the collected probe's `nvidia.gpus.length`. Unavailable inventory defaults conservatively to 1; an empty inventory records 0.
84:  - `concurrency`: the validated `concurrency.json` object (see Concurrency probe), or null when the probe did not run or its output is missing or invalid.
85-  - `host_only`: boolean (U49). True exactly when the profile shows no CUDA activity: the rows `kernels`, `memcpy H2D`, `memcpy D2H` and `CUDA API host time` are all present, each with `wall_s` 0 and `gpu_s` 0 or null, and `gpu_util.json` holds at least one sample and every sample's `util` is 0. Otherwise false, including for profiles without those rows.
86-- Profile facts are `{profile_complete, timed_fraction, gpu_telemetry}` plus common `tokens_known` and `gpu_busy_known`, plus optional `headroom`: the packet's `concurrency.factor` (finite positive ratio) or null, and optional `host_only`: the packet's `host_only` boolean, or null when no packet was written. Every executed profile stage emits `headroom` and `host_only`; both are optional in the v2 schema so older records stay valid, and both are null on SKIPPED/stub records. `profile_complete` is true when the command exits 0 and all three inputs validate, even when the numeric gate fails. The deterministic gate requires at least three stages, no process wrappers, `timed_fraction >= 0.9`, and `gpu_telemetry=true`. A stage is a process wrapper if its name contains a case-insensitive token `process`, `wrapper`, `telemetry`, `total`, or `overall` delimited by whitespace, underscores, hyphens, or string boundaries, or if its `wall_s` is within 2% of `total_wall_s` (inclusive). Any wrapper fails the gate, even alongside three internal stages. In a host-only profile (packet `host_only` true) the `other host time` row is exempt from the 2% test, though not from the name test: the fixed profiler computes it as the wall-time remainder, so with no CUDA activity it is the whole command by construction rather than a wrapper around measured stages. Every other gate condition applies to host-only profiles unchanged, and profiles that are not host-only are gated exactly as before. A host-only profile leaves the pipelining and multi-GPU bounds at 1 (no transfer or compute time); its whole-workload bounds come only from the concurrency probe. Run evidence (blind-01 run9, replayed on its saved files 2026-11-01): the published baseline is CPU-only; Nsight recorded no CUDA kernel, memory or API activity, GPU utilisation was zero in every sample, and `other host time` was the whole command, so the 2% test failed the gate as `numeric` and the concurrency probe never ran. Owner decision 2026-11-01: CPU-only baselines are in scope. Numeric gate failures preserve the packet and use `error_class: numeric`; missing or invalid files use `error_class: parse`. A failed gate or parse stops downstream work without a profile repair.

88:## Concurrency probe: calibration of same-GPU headroom
89-- Purpose: measure, before any prediction or method exists, how much more throughput one GPU gives when the unchanged published command runs several times at once. This measured factor is the only source of same-GPU headroom for bounds. No model call is involved.
90-- When the profile command exits 0 and the profile gate passes, the pipeline uploads trusted `m5/concurrency_probe.py` to remote `profiler/` and, through boxrun as operation `concurrency` with the resolved `profile` budget, runs `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py harness/run_command.sh out/concurrency <budget_s>` from the shared run directory. Remote `out/concurrency/` is cleared first. Fetched files land in `A/results/profile/out/concurrency/`; the log is `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. There is no agent repair and no execution retry. Probe receipts count toward profile v1 `usd` and `gpu_s` like other box receipts.
91-- Each invocation runs `bash harness/run_command.sh` with its working directory set to a fresh `concurrency-work/<label>/` under the shared run directory. That directory holds a symlink to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work` and `evaluation-work`, plus an empty `out/` directory. Labels are `single-1`, `single-2`, `single-3`, `n2-1`, `n2-2`, `n4-1` to `n4-4`. Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<label>.log` of the shared run directory. The environment is inherited unchanged apart from the MPS variables below. Nsight is not used.
92-- MPS: when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is on PATH, the probe starts a user-level daemon (`nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d`) with `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` and `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` set to fresh directories under `concurrency-work/`, passes both variables to every invocation, and stops the daemon (`echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with the same variables) before exiting, including after failures and on SIGTERM. If the daemon fails to start or any invocation fails under MPS, the probe stops the daemon, records `mps_failed: true`, and repeats the complete probe once without MPS in fresh work directories. Without the binary there is no MPS and `mps_failed` is false.
93-- MPS use is verified, not assumed. The daemon's `control.log` in its `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` records each client connection as a line containing `NEW CLIENT <pid> from user <uid>`. After each single run and each batch under MPS, the probe counts these lines (case-sensitive substring `NEW CLIENT `, followed by an integer pid and ` from user `). The count must have grown by at least the number of copies just run (1 for a single run, n for a batch of n). A missing or unreadable log, or a smaller increase, means the copies did not run under MPS: the probe treats this like an invocation failure under MPS (stop the daemon, `mps_failed: true`, repeat the complete probe once without MPS). `mps: true` is therefore recorded only when every counted measurement was verified to run under MPS. No log content enters `concurrency.json`.
94-- Sequence: three single runs one after another, then 2 copies started together, then 4 copies started together. Wall seconds come from a monotonic clock around each subprocess; a batch's wall runs from launching its first copy to the exit of its last. `T1` is the median of the single walls. A single run that exits nonzero stops the probe with a null factor. Before each batch, the batch is skipped when `n * T1` exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. A batch counts only when every copy exits 0. For a counted batch, `factor_n = n * T1 / wall_n`.
95-- `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mps, mps_failed, single_wall_s, batches, factor}`:
96-  - `mps`: boolean, true when the recorded measurements ran under MPS; `mps_failed`: boolean;
97-  - `single_wall_s`: array of exactly three entries, each a finite positive number or null (failed or not run);
98-  - `batches`: exactly two rows, in order n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`; `wall_s` and `factor` are finite positive numbers or null, `all_ok` and `skipped` are booleans, and `factor` is null unless the batch counted;
99-  - `factor`: the largest counted `factor_n`, or null when any single run failed or no batch counted.
100-  The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file, including with a null factor, and 2 when it cannot. It does not check output correctness: it measures throughput only.
101-- The probe never fails the profile stage and never changes the profile gate. A probe timeout, nonzero exit, or missing or invalid file gives packet `concurrency: null` and `headroom: null`. The pipeline validates the file against the exact shape above before copying it into the packet.
102:- Unit mode (U50). When the profile gate passes with packet `host_only` true and `A/harness/` holds both `run_units.sh` and `units.json`, the probe runs in unit mode: `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py --units harness/run_units.sh harness/units.json out/concurrency <budget_s>`, with the same upload, operation, budget, clearing, fetch, log location and no-retry rules as command mode. Otherwise the probe runs in command mode exactly as described above. Unit mode never uses MPS and does not look for the MPS binary. It compares the same four units run in one invocation, as separate invocations one after another, and as separate invocations at once, holding inputs and per-unit configuration fixed and checking every output byte for byte. Owner decision 2026-11-01: the smallest bounded experiment that resolves whether a CPU-only baseline's units gain throughput when run at once, with only the pipeline changes that comparison needs. Reader evidence (blind-01 run9): units are distinct inputs, selectable by a published option with identifiers that are safe as arguments; each unit writes its own result files at the same paths in full and subset runs, with no run-specific content, and its outputs repeat bit for bit; the reproduce logs record every unit's cost; whether a unit reads state left by earlier units of the same invocation is unknown, which the comparison with the frozen baseline tests; units take 1 to 10 min with a cost spread over 50%; the baseline's own threads already use at least half the logical CPUs. Command mode would instead run three whole commands of 1 to 2 h and compare no outputs.
103-- Sample: units sorted by `cost_s` ascending, ties by manifest order; the sample is the four consecutive sorted units starting at sorted position floor((N - 4) / 2), N being the number of units, kept in that order as sample positions 0 to 3. Units near the median cost keep concurrent invocations of similar length, so a batch runs at its full width for nearly its whole wall time; the factor therefore describes typical units, not the shortest or longest.
104-- Arms run in this fixed order, every invocation in a fresh work directory built as in command mode (named `<label>` for an arm with one invocation, `<label>-<j>` for invocation j = 1, 2, ... of an arm with several):
105-  - `a-1`: one invocation `bash harness/run_units.sh <id0> <id1> <id2> <id3>` (sample order), the baseline's own serial mode;
106-  - `b-1`: four invocations of one unit each, one after another in sample order;
107-  - `c2-1`: sample units 0 and 1 started together, then, after both exit, units 2 and 3 started together;
108-  - `c4-1`: all four started together;
109-  - `c4-2`, `c2-2`, `b-2`, `a-2`: the same arms again in reverse order, to balance drift.
110-  Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<work directory name>.log` of the shared run directory, and its environment is inherited unchanged. An arm's wall runs on a monotonic clock from launching its first invocation to the exit of its last.
111-- Output checks. After `a-1`, every output path of every sample unit under `a-1`'s `out/` must be byte-identical to the same path under the shared run directory's `reproduce-out/` (`baseline_match`); a file missing on either side is a mismatch. When `a-1` exits nonzero or `baseline_match` is false, no later arm runs. After every later invocation, its units' output files must be byte-identical to `a-1`'s (`outputs_match`, true when every later executed invocation matched). An arm counts when all of its invocations exit 0 and all of their compared files match.
112-- Budget: before each arm, that arm and every later arm are skipped when its estimate exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. The estimate is the sum of the sample's `cost_s` for `a-1`, and `a-1`'s measured wall for every later arm.
113-- Resource use. For each invocation, from `os.wait4` on its process (which includes its waited-for descendants): `cpu_s` (user plus system seconds), `max_rss_kb`, `nivcsw` (involuntary context switches), `inblock` and `oublock`. For each arm, sampled about once a second while it runs: `busy_fraction` (mean non-idle share of total CPU time from `/proc/stat`, idle including iowait), `mem_available_min_kb` (the minimum `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo`) and `threads_max` (the largest sum of `Threads` from `/proc/<pid>/status` over the processes of the arm's invocations; each invocation starts its own session and process group). An arm's `cpu_s` is the sum over its invocations and `effective_cores` is that sum divided by the arm's wall. Memory bandwidth and caches are not measured.
114-- In unit mode `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mode, mps, mps_failed, outcome, units_total, sample, baseline_match, outputs_match, serial_wall_s, separate_wall_s, batches, arms, nproc, mem_total_kb, factor}`:
115-  - `mode`: `"units"`; `mps` and `mps_failed`: false;
116-  - `outcome`: the first that applies of `"invalid_units"` (manifest unreadable, invalid or with fewer than four units), `"failed"` (an executed invocation exited nonzero), `"baseline_mismatch"`, `"outputs_mismatch"`, `"skipped"` (no `c2` or `c4` arm counted), otherwise `"measured"`;
117-  - `units_total`: N, or null for `invalid_units`; `sample`: four rows `{index, cost_s}` in sample order, `index` being the manifest position, or `[]` for `invalid_units`. No unit identifier or output path appears in the file;
118-  - `baseline_match` and `outputs_match`: booleans, or null when not evaluated;
119-  - `serial_wall_s`: the mean wall of the counted `a` arms; `separate_wall_s`: the mean wall of the counted `b` arms; each a finite positive number or null;
120-  - `batches`: exactly two rows, n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`: `wall_s` is the mean wall of the executed `c<n>` arms or null when none ran, `skipped` is true when none ran, `all_ok` is true when at least one ran and every executed one counted, and `factor` is `serial_wall_s / wall_s` when `all_ok` is true and `outcome` is `measured`, otherwise null;
121-  - `arms`: exactly eight rows in the fixed order, each exactly `{label, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, cpu_s, effective_cores, busy_fraction, mem_available_min_kb, threads_max, invocations}`, with `label` from `a-1` to `a-2`; numbers are finite and nonnegative, or null when the arm did not run; `invocations` lists the executed invocations in launch order, each exactly `{units, rc, wall_s, cpu_s, max_rss_kb, nivcsw, inblock, oublock}`, `units` being sample positions;
122-  - `nproc`: `os.cpu_count()`; `mem_total_kb`: `MemTotal` from `/proc/meminfo`;
123-  - `factor`: the largest non-null batch factor, or null.
124-  The factor compares the baseline's own serial mode with concurrent invocations over the same units, so per-invocation start-up costs count against it; `separate_wall_s` minus `serial_wall_s` shows that cost. The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file and 2 when it cannot.

Bounds and propose read only `factor`, `mps` and `mps_failed`, so they treat a unit-mode factor like a command-mode one, and a measured unit-mode factor below 1.05 is a valid negative finding (`mps` and `mps_failed` both false).

Deterministic runs use one null seed. Stochastic protocols use `{kind:"paired_median", seeds:[unique integers]}` instead; the same seeds apply to both arms. 262-- Metrics have unique nonempty `name`, nonempty `source` and tolerance. Deterministic tolerance is a finite nonnegative absolute number, `{abs:x}` or `{rel:x}`. Each paired row must satisfy `abs(method-baseline) <= tolerance`; relative tolerance multiplies `abs(baseline)`, including exact agreement at zero. All reported metric values must be finite numbers, never booleans.
263-- Stochastic metrics require absolute tolerance. For each metric and seed, average the paired method-minus-baseline differences over fixed inputs. Use an exact sign-test confidence interval for the median of those seed averages. Equivalence requires the entire interval inside `[-tolerance,+tolerance]`, including endpoints. Bonferroni divides the two-sided error probability across sealed metrics. This tests equivalence of the median paired effect defined by the seal; it is not a failure-to-reject difference test.
264-- Confidence is finite in `[0.5,1)`. For sorted samples `x` of length `n`, select the largest `k >= 1` with `P(Binomial(n,0.5) < k) <= alpha/2` for equivalence or `<= alpha` for performance. Equivalence bounds are `[x[k-1],x[n-k]]`; performance uses lower bound `x[k-1]` and an unbounded upper endpoint represented by null. No admissible `k` means insufficient measurements and VOID. At 95%, one metric needs at least six independent seed pairs; performance needs at least five timing pairs. More metrics or greater confidence can require more seeds. No bootstrap randomness or asymptotic approximation is used.
265-- `warmup` is an integer >=0, measured but excluded from performance statistics; `repetitions` is an integer >=5. Each pair contains one run of each arm in independently shuffled order from Python's `random.Random(sealed_seed)`. Warmup pairs and curve arm order use the same RNG stream. Both arms use the same box, sealed inputs, seeds, configuration and scope. Published baseline is never tuned.
266-- `timing_scope.kind` is `process_wall` (trusted `perf_counter` around the complete adapter subprocess) or `reported_wall` (adapter's measured `wall_s`, for scopes requiring program timers). Both arms must echo the exact sealed scope. Adapters must synchronize all used GPUs before completion/timer stop and include launch/transfer/merge overhead required by the scope. Missing or mismatched scope is VOID. Reported timings are actual program measurements, never extrapolated estimates.
267-- `hardware_cost_basis` declares positive integer GPU counts per arm, bounded by both box and probe capacity. `C/box.json.price_usd_h` must be finite and positive. Per-GPU tariff is box hourly price divided by available box GPUs; run USD is measured seconds times GPUs used times this tariff /3600. Pair speedup is baseline seconds / method seconds; `speedup_published` is the median pair speedup. `cost_ratio` is the median paired method-USD / baseline-USD ratio. `equal_cost` means `cost_ratio <= 1`. Performance requires matched scientific outputs on warmups and timed pairs, the sealed one-sided confidence lower bound >= `minimum_worthwhile_gain`, and equal cost. `prediction_ratio` divides median speedup by the selected sealed interval's midpoint. Zero or unavailable pricing cannot establish equal cost.
268-- Curves use GPU-second budgets. Each invocation receives the sealed budget and is bounded by both its script timeout and budget / GPUs used. Allocation seconds include the complete subprocess, even with reported timing. Both arms must finish within the budget and echo it exactly. Each complete budget produces one point with both measured outcomes; no interpolation or extrapolation occurs. `equal_outcome_target` defines a metric, finite numeric `target`, and comparison `==`, `>`, `>=`, `<` or `<=`; each outcome is the mean metric over fixed rows and records `target_achieved`. `uncertainty:{min,max}` reports the observed range, not a confidence interval. A failed or unachieved target is retained. If this benchmark has no outcome curve, seal `{not_applicable:true,reason:"explicit scientific reason"}` instead; `curve_points=0`, `not_applicable=true`.
269-
270-### Baseline and method adapter interface
271-
272:The harness may additionally provide `A/harness/run_evaluation.sh`, uploaded during reproduce. Otherwise the evaluator uses `harness/run_anchors.sh` for baseline evaluation. The baseline adapter must run the exact published configuration. The method adapter is `payload/method/run_method.sh`. For validity, use optional `payload/method/run_anchors.sh`; absent that file, derive the anchor invocation by running `run_method.sh` with `EVAL_MODE=anchors`. Both routes must rerun the complete published anchor protocol under the method and write `out/anchors_measured.json`; copying baseline or published values is forbidden.
273-
274-Every invocation runs in a fresh `evaluation-work/<phase>/<index>/<arm>/` with empty `out/` and links to the fixed `baseline-published/`, `method/`, `data/`, `harness/`, `payload/`, `baseline-out/` trees. This preserves relative paths while separating repetitions. Environment:
275-
276-- `BASELINE_DIR`, `METHOD_DIR`, `BASELINE_OUT`: absolute fixed source/output paths; `METHOD_OUT` and `EVAL_OUT`: this invocation's absolute empty output directory.
277-- `EVAL_ARM`: `baseline` or `method`; `EVAL_MODE`: `anchors`, `equivalence`, `warmup`, `performance`, or `curve`.
278-- `EVAL_PROTOCOL`: absolute path to the complete immutable sealed predictions JSON, including splits, input pins and seeds. `EVAL_INPUTS` and `EVAL_SEEDS` are JSON encodings of `evaluation_inputs` and `paired_seed_tests`. `EVAL_INPUTS` is an object whose `ids` array lists the sealed input identities in order; each record's `input_id` is one of those strings, and every other key (pins, configuration, generated-input descriptions) describes inputs and is never itself an input. `EVAL_SEEDS` is either `{kind:"paired_median",seeds:[integer,...]}`, whose seeds are the execution seeds in order, or `{kind:"deterministic",...}`, whose single execution seed is null; other keys are descriptive. The harness prompt (which writes `run_evaluation.sh` before the seal exists) and the method author prompt both state these two shapes.
279-- `EVAL_COMPUTE_BUDGET`: empty outside curves; numeric budget string for curve runs.
280-
281-Non-anchor adapters write `EVAL_OUT/evaluation.json`:
282-
283-```json
284-{
285-  "records": [{"input_id": "input-0", "seed": null, "metrics": {"accuracy": 0.95}}],
286-  "timing_scope": {"kind": "process_wall", "gpu_synchronization": "adapter", "description": "includes launch, transfer, compute and merge"},
287-  "gpu_count": 1,
288-  "wall_s": 1.2,
289-  "compute_budget": 60
290-}
291-```
292-
293-`records` is required in all non-anchor modes. `wall_s` is required and finite positive only for reported timing. `gpu_count` must match the arm's sealed count. Curves require exact numeric `compute_budget`; it is optional otherwise. Additional program output fields are allowed. Arrays with missing/duplicate/reordered inputs, wrong seeds, unequal counts, or omitted final inputs fail equivalence. Each record's `metrics` holds every sealed `equivalence_metrics` name as a finite number for that input and seed, keyed by exactly that name. The method adapter's records mean the same as the baseline adapter's: for each input and seed, the same workload execution and the same metric definitions; the method author prompt states this. Missing/malformed files or metrics are unavailable measurements, producing VOID. Scripts exit nonzero on execution failure and must not modify baseline, data, frozen outputs/tests, harness, evaluator payload or method source during evaluation.
294-
295-### Evaluation artifacts, provenance and failures
296-
297-- `m5/eval_validity.py`, `eval_equivalence.py`, `eval_performance.py` accept `--stage <validity|equivalence|performance> --in <manifest.json> --out <directory>` (the corresponding stage only; stage flag is optional). `eval_common.py` shares IO, invocation and exact confidence calculations; validity calls `score_anchors.score` unchanged.
298-- Script-owned `C/evaluate/manifest.json` is created exclusively, mode 0444. Existing `C/evaluate/` prevents a new evaluation round. It contains `{remote_directory,protocol,prediction,box,gpu_count,run_timeout_s,method_files,anchors,input_hashes}`. `prediction` is the selected method's sealed prediction. `input_hashes` contains `seal_sha256`, the implementation's baseline/data/output/test/method-payload tree hashes, `anchors_sha256`, local `harness_sha256`, and `evaluators` mapping each uploaded Python filename to its exact-byte SHA-256. Method files must match the reviewed payload. Before/after every scorer, trusted integrity commands recheck source, data, frozen baseline outputs, tests, method payload, built method source, harness, evaluator helpers and manifest. Initial remote hashes additionally freeze method source, harness and evaluator payload for the evaluation round; source/harness modes can differ from local copies. The seal and local frozen tests are rechecked too.
299-- Helpers, manifest and sealed predictions are uploaded in bounded base64 chunks through boxrun. Operations are `evaluate-upload`, `evaluate-state-before-<stage>`, `evaluate-state-after-<stage>`, and `evaluate-<stage>`. Logs and each fetched `out/` remain in `A/results/evaluate/<operation>/`; repeated upload receipts/logs share their operation directory. Remote artifacts are `out/eval/{validity.json,equivalence.json,performance.json,curve.json,raw.jsonl}`. The final fetched evaluation files/logs are also copied directly to `A/results/evaluate/`. `out/evaluate-state.json` contains remote tree hashes. Nothing scientific enters operator signatures.
300-- All verdicts have `status` (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `VOID`) and, once executed, `input_hashes`. `validity.json` adds `validity_pass` and the exact anchor score fields `anchors`, `anchors_passed`, `anchors_total`, `all_passed`. `equivalence.json` adds `equivalence_pass` and `metrics`: deterministic rows `{metric,passed,max_abs_difference}`, stochastic rows `{metric,passed,difference_interval,confidence}`, or a failed alignment row `{passed:false,reason_code:"counts_or_alignment"}`. `performance.json` adds `performance_pass`, `equal_cost`, `speedup_published`, `speedup_tuned:null`, `cost_ratio`, `prediction_ratio`, `confidence`, `speedup_interval`, `matched_outcome`, `pairs`. Each pair has `{index,order,baseline_s,method_s,baseline_gpus,method_gpus,speedup,cost_ratio,baseline_usd,method_usd}`.
301-- `curve.json` has `{status,input_hashes,not_applicable,curve_points,points}`, plus a reason for not-applicable/invalid protocols. Each point has `compute_budget` and `baseline`/`method` objects. Successful arms have `{status:"PASS",outcome,target_achieved,uncertainty,allocated_gpu_hours,usd}`; unavailable arms have `{status:"VOID",outcome:null,reason_code}`. `curve_points` counts budgets with both outcomes measured. Failed budgets remain in `points`; partial successful budgets are saved after every iteration. An unachieved target is a measured outcome, not a missing point.
302-- `raw.jsonl` appends `{phase,index,arm,compute_budget,rc,process_wall_s}` immediately after execution and a second row with `output_sha256` and actual `report` after successful output parsing. Each invocation preserves its `<phase>-<index>-<arm>.log` and parsed `.json` alongside the verdicts. Anchor measurements are saved as `anchors_measured.json`.
303-- Before execution all four local verdicts start as `{status:"VOID",reason_code:"not_run"}`. Scorer parse/missing-output failures write `status:"VOID"`, the corresponding `*_pass:null`, and fixed `reason_code:"missing_or_invalid_measurements"`. Invalid manifests use `invalid_manifest`. Earlier raw/phase evidence is retained. Finite measurements are required: zero placeholders never establish PASS.
304-- Validity uses the same anchor/reference rules: references never fail validity, and with no anchors validity passes when the method arm's anchor protocol exits 0 with a valid measurement file; evaluate's `run_valid` is then null. Validity failure stops immediately: `status:FAIL`, `error_class:anchor`, exit 4 (`exit_kind:anchor`), `run_valid:false`. Nonzero anchor execution also fails validity; absent/invalid anchor files or any missing/non-numeric anchor (not reference) measurement are VOID with `validity_pass:null`, retaining scored rows when available. Equivalence/performance scientific failure uses FAIL, `numeric`, exit 5 (`later_stage`). Infrastructure/fetch/integrity or unavailable measurement failures use VOID, fixed `infra`/`other`/`parse`, exit 2; outer scorer timeout uses `timeout`, exit 3. Missing curves prevent overall PASS; an already measured performance failure retains FAIL/exit 5 while the curve stays VOID. Subsequent verdicts remain independently VOID when not run; no performance result can override invalidity. All failures still proceed to takeaways. A box timeout permits one identical bounded scorer retry; immutable reviewed payloads and sealed protocol cannot be changed during evaluation.
305-- Evaluate facts contain `{validity_pass,equivalence_pass,performance_pass,equal_cost,speedup_published,speedup_tuned,cost_ratio,prediction_ratio,curve_points,tokens_known,gpu_busy_known}`, plus the optional timeout fields defined above. Unavailable values are null, including unmeasured curves; explicitly inapplicable curves have count 0. No model calls means `tokens_known:true`; receipt telemetry owns `gpu_busy_known`. Overall PASS requires three passing verdicts and a complete or explicitly inapplicable curve. Stage stub/SKIPPED facts preserve their existing null contract.
306-- `stage_budgets_s.evaluate` bounds each complete scorer command, default 2400 seconds. Each subprocess uses the resolved method_run budget; uploads/integrity commands use method_setup. Configure budgets for the fixed sealed run count. Boxrun interface and content-free accounting remain unchanged.
307-
308-## Compute metadata
309-- The shared v1 `model_family` enum now also accepts `cursor`: its complete set is `codex`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `lambda`, `claude`, `none`. Each stage uses the answering model in that stage's successful wf journal `result`/`cached` events, not the requested model or failed attempts. A `lambda/` model reports `lambda` despite OpenCode dispatch. With several answering families, the last answer wins; with no successful answer, the value is `none`.
310-- wf exposes `agent.journal`, the absolute journal path. Cached journal events now include `model`, preserved from the successful result in the resume source. Cached answers retain model provenance but incur no new token usage. Failed attempts and unused shadow answers do not replace the answering family.
311-- New `C/stages/<stage>.json` receipts contain `{stage, status, wall_s, gpu_s, usd, model_family, notes}`, plus any stage-provided v1 overrides and measured token counts. Stage/status/model families use their existing enums. `notes` is an array with either no entries or the single fixed code `multiple_model_families`; no model text, prompts, filenames, or scientific facts are copied into it. These receipts are separate from `C/receipts/` box command receipts.
312-- Both serve and dev `lambda_serve.sh up` write `$HOME/.cache/metis-serve/box.json` atomically alongside `state.json`. Its keys are `{type, region, price_usd_h, started_utc}`: Lambda instance-type and region identifiers, a numeric hourly USD price, and a UTC ISO timestamp. Repeated state saves preserve the allocation's start. Confirmed `down` retains `box.json` and adds `ended_utc` (UTC ISO timestamp) and `hours` (nonnegative elapsed allocation hours, including startup and termination polling). State archival behavior is unchanged. The next `up` replaces this record for the new allocation.
313-- At the start of reproduce, the pipeline copies the current shared `box.json` to `C/box.json`, replacing any stale run copy. Missing box metadata leaves pricing unavailable and stage USD at zero. At takeaways, a matching allocation record can refresh the copy with its confirmed end; a different allocation never replaces the snapshot. If reproduce was skipped, takeaways snapshots the current allocation to account for any run overlap.
314-- Box receipts add numeric nonnegative `gpu_busy_s` and boolean `gpu_busy_known`. The detached remote script writes `<receipt-id>.gpu` beside its log, sampling `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits` immediately and every 2 seconds until the command exits or times out. Each finite utilization sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100 * 2` seconds; samples from every GPU are summed. Missing/invalid samples contribute nothing. No valid samples means `gpu_busy_s=0`, `gpu_busy_known=false`. Telemetry collection failure does not change command/fetch success. Sampling survives loss of the local polling process; the remote runner stops sampling before publishing its exit marker.
315-- Stage v1 `gpu_s` sums its box receipts' `gpu_busy_s`, including failed commands and retries. For stages with box receipts, `facts.gpu_busy_known` is true only when every receipt has valid busy telemetry; partial telemetry contributes its measured values while the flag stays false. Harness profile timing remains separate evidence and never substitutes for receipt GPU accounting. This supersedes the earlier statement that reproduce/profile always leave this flag false.
316-- Stage v1 `usd` is `sum(its box receipts' wall_s) / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h`, including uploads, probes, failed commands, polling/fetch time, and retries. Stage `wall_s` remains elapsed stage time and includes agent calls. No allocation or model-call envelopes are added.
317-- Takeaways facts optionally add `run_box_usd`, a finite nonnegative number or null; old v2 records without this key remain valid. The pipeline writes null for a SKIPPED takeaways stage; otherwise it writes the whole run's box charge here: the intersection of `[run start, takeaways accounting time]` with `[box.started_utc, box.ended_utc]`, multiplied by hourly price. An active box uses accounting time as its end. When timestamps or price are unavailable, it falls back to summed stage USD. This is a run summary, not extra stage spend; takeaways v1 `usd` retains only its own command attribution.
318-- `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` now has a Compute section: one row per stage with existing gate columns plus `wall_s`, `gpu_s`, `usd`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `model_family`; a box table; and run totals. The optional Python API is now `takeaway(records, raid=None, box=None)`. The CLI reads only validated signatures and sibling `C/box.json`; it does not read agent content. Run USD uses `facts.run_box_usd` when present, avoiding double-counting stage attribution; other totals preserve the existing launch/model-call preference and stage fallback.
319-- Operator box output whitelists only `type` and `price_usd_h`. Price must be a finite nonnegative JSON number (never a boolean); unavailable price renders `null`. Type is a fixed enum: `gpu_1x_a10`, `gpu_1x_a100`, `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4`, `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4_80gb`, `gpu_8x_a100`, `gpu_8x_a100_80gb_sxm4`, `gpu_1x_h100_pcie`, `gpu_1x_h100_sxm5`, `gpu_8x_h100_sxm5`, `gpu_1x_gh200`, `gpu_1x_h200`, `gpu_8x_h200_sxm5`, `gpu_1x_b200`, `gpu_8x_b200`, or `unknown`. Unknown types render `unknown`; region, timestamps, and all other box fields never enter operator output.

    88	## Concurrency probe: calibration of same-GPU headroom
    89	- Purpose: measure, before any prediction or method exists, how much more throughput one GPU gives when the unchanged published command runs several times at once. This measured factor is the only source of same-GPU headroom for bounds. No model call is involved.
    90	- When the profile command exits 0 and the profile gate passes, the pipeline uploads trusted `m5/concurrency_probe.py` to remote `profiler/` and, through boxrun as operation `concurrency` with the resolved `profile` budget, runs `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py harness/run_command.sh out/concurrency <budget_s>` from the shared run directory. Remote `out/concurrency/` is cleared first. Fetched files land in `A/results/profile/out/concurrency/`; the log is `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. There is no agent repair and no execution retry. Probe receipts count toward profile v1 `usd` and `gpu_s` like other box receipts.
    91	- Each invocation runs `bash harness/run_command.sh` with its working directory set to a fresh `concurrency-work/<label>/` under the shared run directory. That directory holds a symlink to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work` and `evaluation-work`, plus an empty `out/` directory. Labels are `single-1`, `single-2`, `single-3`, `n2-1`, `n2-2`, `n4-1` to `n4-4`. Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<label>.log` of the shared run directory. The environment is inherited unchanged apart from the MPS variables below. Nsight is not used.
    92	- MPS: when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is on PATH, the probe starts a user-level daemon (`nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d`) with `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` and `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` set to fresh directories under `concurrency-work/`, passes both variables to every invocation, and stops the daemon (`echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with the same variables) before exiting, including after failures and on SIGTERM. If the daemon fails to start or any invocation fails under MPS, the probe stops the daemon, records `mps_failed: true`, and repeats the complete probe once without MPS in fresh work directories. Without the binary there is no MPS and `mps_failed` is false.
    93	- MPS use is verified, not assumed. The daemon's `control.log` in its `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` records each client connection as a line containing `NEW CLIENT <pid> from user <uid>`. After each single run and each batch under MPS, the probe counts these lines (case-sensitive substring `NEW CLIENT `, followed by an integer pid and ` from user `). The count must have grown by at least the number of copies just run (1 for a single run, n for a batch of n). A missing or unreadable log, or a smaller increase, means the copies did not run under MPS: the probe treats this like an invocation failure under MPS (stop the daemon, `mps_failed: true`, repeat the complete probe once without MPS). `mps: true` is therefore recorded only when every counted measurement was verified to run under MPS. No log content enters `concurrency.json`.
    94	- Sequence: three single runs one after another, then 2 copies started together, then 4 copies started together. Wall seconds come from a monotonic clock around each subprocess; a batch's wall runs from launching its first copy to the exit of its last. `T1` is the median of the single walls. A single run that exits nonzero stops the probe with a null factor. Before each batch, the batch is skipped when `n * T1` exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. A batch counts only when every copy exits 0. For a counted batch, `factor_n = n * T1 / wall_n`.
    95	- `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mps, mps_failed, single_wall_s, batches, factor}`:
    96	  - `mps`: boolean, true when the recorded measurements ran under MPS; `mps_failed`: boolean;
    97	  - `single_wall_s`: array of exactly three entries, each a finite positive number or null (failed or not run);
    98	  - `batches`: exactly two rows, in order n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`; `wall_s` and `factor` are finite positive numbers or null, `all_ok` and `skipped` are booleans, and `factor` is null unless the batch counted;
    99	  - `factor`: the largest counted `factor_n`, or null when any single run failed or no batch counted.
   100	  The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file, including with a null factor, and 2 when it cannot. It does not check output correctness: it measures throughput only.
   101	- The probe never fails the profile stage and never changes the profile gate. A probe timeout, nonzero exit, or missing or invalid file gives packet `concurrency: null` and `headroom: null`. The pipeline validates the file against the exact shape above before copying it into the packet.
   102	- Unit mode (U50). When the profile gate passes with packet `host_only` true and `A/harness/` holds both `run_units.sh` and `units.json`, the probe runs in unit mode: `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py --units harness/run_units.sh harness/units.json out/concurrency <budget_s>`, with the same upload, operation, budget, clearing, fetch, log location and no-retry rules as command mode. Otherwise the probe runs in command mode exactly as described above. Unit mode never uses MPS and does not look for the MPS binary. It compares the same four units run in one invocation, as separate invocations one after another, and as separate invocations at once, holding inputs and per-unit configuration fixed and checking every output byte for byte. Owner decision 2026-11-01: the smallest bounded experiment that resolves whether a CPU-only baseline's units gain throughput when run at once, with only the pipeline changes that comparison needs. Reader evidence (blind-01 run9): units are distinct inputs, selectable by a published option with identifiers that are safe as arguments; each unit writes its own result files at the same paths in full and subset runs, with no run-specific content, and its outputs repeat bit for bit; the reproduce logs record every unit's cost; whether a unit reads state left by earlier units of the same invocation is unknown, which the comparison with the frozen baseline tests; units take 1 to 10 min with a cost spread over 50%; the baseline's own threads already use at least half the logical CPUs. Command mode would instead run three whole commands of 1 to 2 h and compare no outputs.
   103	- Sample: units sorted by `cost_s` ascending, ties by manifest order; the sample is the four consecutive sorted units starting at sorted position floor((N - 4) / 2), N being the number of units, kept in that order as sample positions 0 to 3. Units near the median cost keep concurrent invocations of similar length, so a batch runs at its full width for nearly its whole wall time; the factor therefore describes typical units, not the shortest or longest.
   104	- Arms run in this fixed order, every invocation in a fresh work directory built as in command mode (named `<label>` for an arm with one invocation, `<label>-<j>` for invocation j = 1, 2, ... of an arm with several):
   105	  - `a-1`: one invocation `bash harness/run_units.sh <id0> <id1> <id2> <id3>` (sample order), the baseline's own serial mode;
   106	  - `b-1`: four invocations of one unit each, one after another in sample order;
   107	  - `c2-1`: sample units 0 and 1 started together, then, after both exit, units 2 and 3 started together;
   108	  - `c4-1`: all four started together;
   109	  - `c4-2`, `c2-2`, `b-2`, `a-2`: the same arms again in reverse order, to balance drift.
